tagline: One stroke each. The picture only exists because you opened the same file.
description:
One stroke each. The invite is the studio. The doodle lives in the file. No account.

A blank page. You draw one line — a curve, a scribble, a secret — then the turn passes. Nobody else may draw until you lift your finger and send it. After a round, you vote on a title from a handful of suggestions, or write your own. Then the picture plays back as a loop of the strokes arriving, in order.

On your own it is you against the page: one stroke at a time, a stack of lines, a tiny looping doodle that stays inside this file. Close it, open it later, the picture is where you left it.

Want a studio? Press Play with friends, then press Invite (in the GifOS menu) and send the link. Everyone who opens it sits around the same page. Whose turn it is is obvious. You cannot draw when it is not your turn. There is no lobby code and no game server. The room is the link.

This is not a whiteboard. A whiteboard lets anyone draw anything, anytime. One Stroke is the constraint — one line each — so the picture can only exist because several people opened the same file.
